extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and higher education administrators), Title IX coordinators, campus legal counsel, OCR reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and compliance standards for a recipient's grievance process under 34 CFR §106.45, describing how schools must treat complainants and respondents, procedural protections, confidentiality/retaliation rules, supportive measures, and OCR enforcement. Focused on institutional implementation and adherence to the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(a) — Treatment of a complainant or respondent may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: States that how a recipient treats a complainant, or a respondent, “may” constitute sex discrimination under Title IX and advises recipients to avoid sex-discriminatory practices during the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies equally to complainants and respondents; cautions recipients not to treat a party differently on the basis of sex. Examples include investigating complaints brought by women but not men, or imposing different sanctions by sex; the provision is intentionally broad (the Department declined to add limiting modifiers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory §106.45(b) — Equal application of grievance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any grievance process rules a recipient chooses to adopt (that are not required under §106.45) must treat the parties equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain discretion to adopt rules (e.g., for orderly hearings) but must apply them without different treatment on the basis of sex; the revision emphasizes treating complainants and respondents equally for rules not otherwise mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(b)(1)(i) — Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents (remedies and sanctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires treating complainants and respondents equitably in the context of Title IX sexual harassment (recognizing that equitable treatment may differ from strict equality with respect to remedies and sanctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants should receive remedies designed to restore or preserve access to education; respondents should not be punished prior to the conclusion of a fair process. The Department added “or other actions that are not supportive measures as defined in §106.30” to clarify scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal appeal rights (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties are expressly permitted to appeal a determination regarding responsibility on the basis of procedural irregularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal rights apply equally to complainants and respondents; additionally, either party may file an OCR complaint about failure to follow §106.45 procedures regardless of whether the violation also amounted to sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to inspect and review evidence (§106.45(b)(5)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires that the parties have equal opportunity to inspect and review evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision guards against one-sided evidence access and ties into other confidentiality/sharing concerns; actions that give one party greater access may violate §106.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility for respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: A presumption of non-responsibility applies to respondents until the conclusion of a fair process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural protection applies only to respondents; it is one of the limited provisions that treats parties differently in recognition of differing interests in remedies versus sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from questions/evidence regarding sexual history for complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants are protected from questions and evidence regarding their sexual history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a complainant-specific protection (an exception to strict equality) intended to prevent re-traumatization and irrelevant inquiry into sexual history.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.71 — Prohibition on retaliation and confidentiality of identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits retaliation and requires recipients to keep confidential the identity of any individual who has made a report or complaint of sex discrimination (including complainants, respondents, witnesses), except as permitted by FERPA, required by law, or necessary to conduct the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints alleging retaliation may be filed according to the prompt and equitable grievance procedures under §106.8(c). The confidentiality requirement has limited, enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures — notice, offer, and explanation (§106.44(a) and §106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify complainants of the availability of supportive measures with or without the filing of a formal complaint, offer supportive measures to the complainant, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be non-punitive and non-disciplinary and cannot unreasonably burden the other party. The final regs clarify recipients have wide latitude to provide supportive measures even when refraining from disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal standard (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may remove a respondent from the recipient's education program or activity without undergoing a grievance process when an individualized safety and risk assessment shows the respondent poses a threat to any person's physical health or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-removal the respondent must be afforded notice and an opportunity to challenge the removal decision; emergency removal is distinct from disciplinary sanction and is allowed to protect safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process must be consistent, fair, reliable, and tailored to Title IX sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department determined that the longstanding regulatory phrase “prompt and equitable” did not prescribe a consistent, fair, reliable grievance process for resolving allegations of Title IX sexual harassment, so the final regulations set forth a specific grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is administrative and aimed at producing factually reliable resolutions of sexual harassment allegations under Title IX; it is not intended to adjudicate criminal charges and does not reflect ‘rape exceptionalism.’

rubrics_metrics.name: No creation of new private rights or protected class
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45 does not create new individual rights or turn respondents into a protected class; it prescribes procedures designed to protect rights already granted under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department enforces compliance administratively; the existence or absence of a private right of action in court does not obviate the Department's authority to promulgate and enforce these regulatory procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR enforcement independent of courts' private-right standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party who believes a recipient failed to follow §106.45 may file a complaint with OCR, which could require the recipient to come into compliance regardless of whether courts would find sex discrimination in a private suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A violation of §106.45 need not equate to sex discrimination to trigger administrative enforcement; OCR can enforce procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for complainants must be designed to restore or preserve access
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies provided to complainants must be “designed to restore or preserve access” to the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters viewed this phrasing as too narrow; Department retained it as the standard for remedies intended to address sex discrimination's impact on educational access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of sex-discriminatory practices to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department identifies examples of treatment that may constitute sex discrimination in a grievance process (e.g., investigating complaints by women but not men; imposing expulsion on female respondents but suspension on male respondents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate how differential treatment by sex may violate §106.45(a); the Department declined to narrowly define or enumerate all such circumstances so as to retain the broad non-discrimination mandate.
